# 2 Samuel Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 183v–184v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_014_page_001.jpg, 2SA_014_page_002.jpg, 2SA_014_page_003.jpg

---

**14:1** And-knew Yo'av son of-Tseruyah that [the]-heart of-the-king [was] upon Avshalom.

**14:2** And-sent Yo'av to-Teqoa and-took from-there a-woman wise [chakhamah], and-said to-her, "Mourn, please, and-put-on, please, garments of-mourning, and-do-not anoint-yourself [with]-oil, and-you-shall-be as-a-woman these many days mourning over a-dead-one.

**14:3** And-you-shall-come to the-king and-speak to-him according-to-this word." And-put Yo'av the-words in-her-mouth.

**14:4** And-said the-woman of-Teqoa to the-king, and-she-fell upon her-face to-the-ground and-bowed-down and-said, "Save [hoshi'ah], O-the-king!"

**14:5** And-said to-her the-king, "What [is]-to-you?" And-she-said, "Indeed [aval], a-woman widow [am]-I, and-died my-husband.

**14:6** And-to-your-maidservant [were]-two sons, and-fought the-two-of-them in-the-field, and-there-was-no rescuer [mattsil] between-them, and-struck the-one the-other and-killed-him.

**14:7** And-behold, risen [has] all the-clan [mishpachah] against your-maidservant and-they-say, 'Give-over [the]-striker of-his-brother, and-we-will-kill-him for-[the]-life [nefesh] of-his-brother whom he-killed, and-we-will-destroy also the-heir [yoresh].' And-they-would-extinguish my-coal [gachalti] that remains, so-as-not to-set to-my-husband a-name and-a-remnant [she'erit] upon [the]-face of-the-ground."

**14:8** And-said the-king to the-woman, "Go to-your-house, and-I will-command concerning-you."

**14:9** And-said the-woman of-Teqoa to the-king, "Upon-me, my-lord the-king, [be]-the-iniquity ['avon], and-upon [the]-house of-my-father; and-the-king and-his-throne [be]-innocent [naqiy]."

**14:10** And-said the-king, "The-one-speaking to-you, bring-him to-me, and-not he-will-add again to-touch you."

**14:11** And-she-said, "Let-remember, please, the-king YHWH your-God, from-multiplying [the]-avenger of-blood [go'el ha-dam] to-destroy, and-let-them-not destroy my-son." And-he-said, "As-lives YHWH, not shall-fall from-[the]-hair of-your-son to-the-ground."

**14:12** And-said the-woman, "Let-speak, please, your-maidservant to my-lord the-king a-word." And-he-said, "Speak."

**14:13** And-said the-woman, "And-why have-you-devised [chashavta] thus against [the]-people of-God? And-from-speaking the-king this word [he-is]-as-guilty ['ashem], in-that-not the-king brings-back his-banished-one [niddacho].

**14:14** For dying we-shall-die [mot namut], and-[we-are]-as-the-water poured-out upon the-ground, that cannot be-gathered-back. And-not does-God take-away a-life [nefesh], but-he-devises plans [machashavot] so-that-not be-banished from-him [the]-banished-one [niddach].

**14:15** And-now that I-have-come to-speak to the-king my-lord this word, [it-is]-because the-people frightened-me, and-said your-maidservant, 'Let-me-speak, please, to the-king; perhaps the-king will-do [the]-word of-his-maidservant.

**14:16** For the-king will-hear, to-deliver his-maidservant from-[the]-hand of-the-man [who-would]-destroy me and my-son together from-[the]-inheritance [nachalah] of-God.'

**14:17** And-said your-maidservant, 'Let-be, please, [the]-word of-my-lord the-king for-rest [limnuchah], for as-[the]-angel [mal'akh] of-God so [is] my-lord the-king, to-hear the-good and-the-evil. And-YHWH your-God will-be with-you.'"

**14:18** And-answered the-king and-said to the-woman, "Do-not-hide, please, from-me a-thing that I [am]-asking you." And-said the-woman, "Let-speak, please, my-lord the-king."

**14:19** And-said the-king, "Is-the-hand of-Yo'av with-you in-all this?" And-answered the-woman and-said, "As-lives your-soul [nafshekha], my-lord the-king, there-is-no [turning]-right or-left from-all that spoke my-lord the-king. For your-servant Yo'av, he commanded-me, and-he put in-[the]-mouth of-your-maidservant all these words.

**14:20** In-order to-turn-around [the]-face of-the-matter, your-servant Yo'av did this thing. And-my-lord [is]-wise, as-[the]-wisdom of-[the]-angel of-God, to-know all that [is] in-the-earth."

**14:21** And-said the-king to Yo'av, "Behold, please, I-have-done this thing. Go, bring-back the-youth, Avshalom."

**14:22** And-fell Yo'av upon his-face to-the-ground and-bowed-down and-blessed the-king. And-said Yo'av, "Today knows your-servant that I-have-found favor [chen] in-your-eyes, my-lord the-king, in-that the-king has-done [the]-word of-his-servant."

**14:23** And-rose-up Yo'av and-went to-Geshur and-brought Avshalom to-Yerushalayim.

**14:24** And-said the-king, "Let-him-turn to his-house, and-my-face let-him-not see." And-turned Avshalom to his-house, and-[the]-face of-the-king he-did-not see.

**14:25** And-as-Avshalom there-was-not a-man beautiful [yafeh] in-all Yisra'el, to-praise exceedingly. From-[the]-sole of-his-foot and-to his-crown [qodqodo] there-was not in-him a-blemish [mum].

**14:26** And-when-he-shaved his-head — and-it-was at-[the]-end of-days to-days [miyamim le-yamim] that he-shaved-it, for it-was-heavy upon-him, and-he-shaved-it — and-he-weighed [the]-hair of-his-head, two-hundred sheqels by-[the]-stone of-the-king.

**14:27** And-were-born to-Avshalom three sons and-one daughter, and-her-name [was] Tamar. She was a-woman beautiful of-appearance [yefat-mar'eh].

**14:28** And-sat Avshalom in-Yerushalayim two years of-days, and-[the]-face of-the-king he-did-not see.

**14:29** And-sent Avshalom to Yo'av, to-send-him to the-king, and-not he-was-willing to-come to-him. And-he-sent again a-second-[time], and-not he-was-willing to-come.

**14:30** And-he-said to his-servants, "See, [the]-portion of-Yo'av [is] near-my-hand [el-yadiy], and-to-him [is]-there barley. Go and-set-it-on-fire [with]-fire." And-set-on-fire [the]-servants of-Avshalom the-portion [with]-fire.

**14:31** And-rose-up Yo'av and-came to Avshalom to-the-house and-said to-him, "Why have-set-on-fire your-servants the-portion that-[is]-to-me [with]-fire?"

**14:32** And-said Avshalom to Yo'av, "Behold, I-sent to-you, saying, 'Come here, and-I-will-send-you to the-king, to-say, "Why did-I-come from-Geshur? Good for-me [while]-I [was]-still there."' And-now, let-me-see [the]-face of-the-king, and-if there-is in-me iniquity ['avon], then-let-him-kill-me."

**14:33** And-came Yo'av to the-king and-told him. And-he-called to-Avshalom, and-he-came to the-king and-bowed-down to-him upon his-face to-the-ground before the-king. And-kissed the-king Avshalom.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — lev ha-melekh al Avshalom:** "The heart of the king was upon/toward Absalom." The preposition *'al* is ambiguous — it could indicate David's heart was "against" Absalom (i.e., still angry) or "upon/toward" him (i.e., longing for him). Context from 13:39 suggests longing. Joab reads the king's heart.

**v.7 — gachalti:** "My coal" — a stunning metaphor. The remaining son is the last ember of the family line. The clan seeks to extinguish this last coal, leaving neither name nor remnant. The metaphor of a single burning coal about to be snuffed out is among the most vivid images of endangered lineage in the Hebrew Bible.

**v.13 — ke-'ashem:** The woman turns the parable to its real target: by not restoring Absalom, David acts as a guilty party against "the people of God." The word *niddach* (banished one) echoes Deuteronomy 30:4, where God promises to gather the *niddachim* (scattered ones).

**v.14 — mot namut:** The infinitive absolute construction "dying we shall die" emphasizes the universality and certainty of death. The theological heart of the woman's argument: we all die; God himself devises ways to bring back the banished; therefore the king should do the same.

**v.17 — mal'akh ha-elohim:** The woman compares the king to "an angel of God" in his capacity to discern good and evil. This is both flattery and theological argument — the king should exercise divine-like mercy alongside divine-like discernment.

**v.26 — two hundred sheqels:** Approximately 2.3 kg (5 lbs) of hair by the royal standard. This detail — seemingly trivial — establishes Absalom's extraordinary physical presence and foreshadows 18:9, where his abundant hair will be his undoing.

**v.27 — Tamar:** Absalom names his daughter after his violated sister, keeping the memory of injustice alive in his own household. The narrator notes that she too was beautiful (*yefat-mar'eh*) — an echo that is both tribute and warning.

*— EMET*
